title: Clarence Williams' publishing house in Chicago
summary: He recalls Clarence Williams' publishing house on State Street, with six people mailing sheet music nationwide.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah. He had a publishing house here down on State, about 35th and State Street for a while. Who? Clarence Williams.

No, he had a place, no. That was real early though, maybe before you moved here. 4th Street, baby, right by Beckers. Huh? Right where Rod Pomer was staying, by Beckers. Clarence Williams, yeah. Yeah, Clarence Williams. He had six people working for him in that place.
I thought you were in Clarence Jones.
One time Clarence Williams did have a publishing house here at your music store.

Oh yeah. 44th and State. And he had six people working for him. And most of them ranges, and you would be surprised to think of the business that he did in that place with six people working. A lot of business. Sending music, just mailing music all over the country. See? Ain't but the one thing, he had a little bad luck, mishap along with it. Now he's got back on his feet again, last time I heard from him.
